subject: CONTINUE statement
notes: Re-read the format in specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 23190 and validated it mechanically (`cite.py --check 14.9.9.2 "CONTINUE"` -> OK, returning the whole format line). Derived expectation BEFORE reading code, from the repaired Figure-notes block: CONTINUE is a required word (the printed missing underline is the C2 typo), the bracket makes the whole phrase optional, and AFTER / SECONDS carry underline rules so they are REQUIRED inside the phrase; the operand is arithmetic-expression-1 (a full 8.8.1 arithmetic expression, not a mere identifier/literal). READ: `continueStatement : CONTINUE (AFTER arithmeticExpression SECONDS)? ;` (CobolControlFlow.g4:361-363). Token-for-token identical to the derived shape: CONTINUE mandatory (so `AFTER 5 SECONDS` alone cannot parse as a CONTINUE, the Figure-notes' second argument), the group is `( ... )?` (bracket), AFTER and SECONDS are hard tokens inside it (not `AFTER?` / `SECONDS?`), so `CONTINUE 5` is rejected. The operand nonterminal is the SHARED `arithmeticExpression` (CobolExpressions.g4:208 -> additiveExpression -> multiplicative -> power), i.e. the same 8.8.1 rule PERFORM VARYING uses, so a parenthesized/compound expression, a literal, an identifier and a function reference are all admitted -- not a narrowed operand. The page-604-vs-page-732 'contradiction' this note once recorded is no contradiction: 8.3.2.4.3 judges optional words within EACH format, so this format's AFTER and SECONDS stay required here while RECEIVE's own CONTINUE phrase (14.9.31.2, p732) leaves them plain (kb/Work PB3751). Wired into the single `statement` rule at CobolParserCore.g4:719. EDITION (derived from Annex E, NOT from the registry's own IntroducedIn column): Annex E.3.3 item 14 at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:43957 -- "Additional functionality added to the CONTINUE statement. The CONTINUE statement has been enhanced to provide the ability to pause runtime execution for a specified period of time" -- so the bracketed phrase is 2023-only while bare CONTINUE is 85-continuous. The compiler gates exactly that split: VersionConformancePass.VisitContinueStatement fires COBOL0900 only when `ctx.arithmeticExpression()` is present (Validation/VersionConformancePass.cs:584-589), i.e. on the PHRASE, never on the verb -- confirmed by 85/wavef_dbg_proc.cob and 85/index_name_r7_windows.cob compiling bare CONTINUE at --std 85. TESTED: 2023/continue_after exercises both operand forms (a literal `AFTER 0` and a data item `AFTER WS-N`); the constructs.json row `continue-after-2023` drives VersionMatrixTests.Construct_MatchesEditionExpectation and IntroducedConstruct_IsRejectedUnderPermissive, so the below-2023 rejection is asserted at 85/2002/2014 and is not waived by --permissive. NOT exercised anywhere: a COMPOUND arithmetic-expression-1 (`CONTINUE AFTER N + 1 SECONDS`); that is a shared-nonterminal reuse rather than a private parse, so it does not cost the verdict. || UPHELD (independent re-derivation): I re-ran all three cite checks myself -- `cite.py --check 14.9.9.2 "CONTINUE"` -> OK (General format), and read the format + Figure notes at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:23189-23212 before opening any code. I re-read CobolControlFlow.g4:361-363 and CobolParserCore.g4:719 directly. I additionally checked the two edges the adjudicator did not: (a) `unaryExpression : addOp unaryExpression | primaryExpression` (CobolExpressions.g4) admits a LEADING SIGN, so `CONTINUE AFTER -1 SECONDS` -- the literal spelling of the GR1a negative case -- parses, and `primaryExpression` admits numericLiteral / ZERO_ARITH / functionCall / dataReference / `( arithmeticExpression )`, so the operand really is the full 8.8.1 rule; (b) the SECONDS terminator cannot be swallowed by the operand, because `additiveExpression` stops at a non-addOp token and `dataReference` is single-word except for OF/IN qualification. I verified the test-refs are LIVE rather than merely present: tests/conformance/2023/manifest.json lists `continue_after` at enabled[22], and tests/WiseOwl.Cobol.Tests.Conformance/VersionMatrixTests.cs:79/:124 are the two named methods; the constructs.json row `continue-after-2023` carries source `CONTINUE AFTER 0 SECONDS.` with expectDiagnostic COBOL0900. || REFUTED (edition-basis citation, verdict unchanged): the adjudicator wrote "E.2's new-reserved-word list at :43951 adds SECONDS". That is WRONG on both counts and I did not inherit it. Line 43951 sits inside Annex **E.3.3 item 13** (heading at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:43225 `E.3.3 Not affecting`), whose lead sentence is "**Context-sensitive words.** In order to provide enhanced functionality, the following words have either been added to the list of context-sensitive words or the context in which they are reserved has been expanded" -- SECONDS is in the CONTEXT-SENSITIVE list, not a reserved-word list. The 8.10 context-sensitive-words table at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:9578 confirms it: `| SECONDS | RETRY phrase, CONTINUE statement |`. The compiler agrees with the STANDARD and not with the adjudicator's note: CobolLexer.g4:562-568 comments SECONDS as "8.10 context-sensitive (user-legal at every edition)" and CobolWords.g4:89 re-admits it as a user word. This does not move the verdict -- the AFTER phrase's 2023 introduction rests on E.3.3 item 14, which I checked and which stands -- but the note's edition evidence was an uncited (and false) claim, exactly the failure mode CLAUDE.md rule 1 names, and is replaced above. || kb/Work PB3751 (2026-10-25): re-affirmed on the changed text — the transcription's figure now underlines CONTINUE, as its own C2 correction note always said it did; the words and the verdict are unchanged (continueStatement : CONTINUE (AFTER arithmeticExpression SECONDS)?).
